blueprint_topic: Management of Care — RN longitudinal heart-failure follow-up, self-care support, and team coordination
stem: A nurse in a multidisciplinary heart-failure clinic is following a client after hospital discharge. Which action best reflects the RN's role in longitudinal heart-failure management?

options.A: Assess symptoms and self-care barriers, reinforce the medication and monitoring plan, and coordinate concerns with the heart-failure team and follow-up services.
options.B: Review the medication and self-care plan, then defer symptom assessment to the next prescriber visit because treatment decisions may change.
options.C: Assess symptoms and arrange follow-up, but leave adherence and self-care education to pharmacy so team responsibilities remain separate.
options.D: Provide self-care teaching and routine follow-up scheduling, then wait to address new nonurgent symptom changes at the planned follow-up visit.

rationale: A is correct. The current AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline describes HF care as ideally multidisciplinary and specifically includes nurses on the team. Its self-care section emphasizes treatment adherence, monitoring for signs and symptoms of worsening HF, and knowing what to do when symptoms occur. Its transitions/team-based-care section describes case management and multidisciplinary coordination across settings, including education, self-management support, medication optimization, weight/symptom monitoring, facilitated access to care during decompensation, and follow-up planning. B is incorrect because symptom assessment is part of nursing assessment and longitudinal HF follow-up rather than something that should be deferred simply because treatment decisions may require another team member. C is incorrect because self-care and medication-adherence education are explicit components of HF multidisciplinary care and are not excluded from the nursing role. D is incorrect because new symptom changes should be assessed and coordinated with the team rather than automatically deferred to a routine future visit.
educational_objective: In longitudinal heart-failure care, the RN should assess symptoms and self-care barriers, reinforce adherence and monitoring education, and coordinate unresolved or worsening concerns with the multidisciplinary team and follow-up services.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America; National Council of State Boards of Nursing
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: HF guideline published April 1, 2022 and still listed on the current ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub when rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029
source_locator: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline — Section 7.1.1 Self-Care Support in HF: HF care is ideally provided by multidisciplinary teams including nurses; self-care includes treatment adherence, symptom monitoring, and understanding what to do when symptoms worsen. Section 9.6 Integration of Care: Transitions and Team-Based Approaches: HF disease-management programs may include HF nurses; case management and multidisciplinary interventions coordinate care across settings and can include education, self-management, medication optimization, weight monitoring, facilitated access during decompensation, and social/psychological support. Table 25 includes reinforcing HF education, assessing adherence, safety monitoring, and coordinating postdischarge care. ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub continues to list the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline as the current HF guideline resource. NCSBN 2026 Test Plan — Management of Care, Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team/Concepts of Management/Continuity of Care, PDF page 24/file page 25: report significant information to other disciplines, ensure continuity across disciplines, identify/collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, act as liaison/coordinator, and follow up unresolved client-care issues.
source_claim_supported: Current HF guidance supports a nursing role within multidisciplinary longitudinal care that includes symptom and self-care assessment, adherence/education support, monitoring, case management, and coordination across settings; NCSBN independently supports RN collaboration, coordination, and follow-up of unresolved care issues.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Concepts of Management, and Continuity of Care, PDF page 24/file page 25: identify significant information to report to other disciplines; review plan of care for continuity; collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; act as liaison/coordinate or manage care; follow up unresolved client-care issues.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care content on PDF page 24/file page 25 was visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20; no CACHE MISS for this locator. The HF guideline was verified through current HTML/ACC hub pages; no PDF is relied upon for the item.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'heart failure nurse longitudinal follow-up self care symptoms multidisciplinary team medication adherence' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the longitudinal HF nursing construct but removed the universal independent-prescribing distractor and rebuilt all alternatives around realistic role-boundary and sequencing errors. Adversarial reread then shortened the correct option and removed an emergency-threshold cue from D so all four choices remain balanced and clinically plausible.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly integrates guideline-supported symptom/self-care assessment, adherence education, monitoring, and multidisciplinary coordination without claiming independent prescribing authority.
option_audit.B: Plausible role-boundary error; incorrect because nursing assessment of symptom change should not be deferred merely because another clinician may make treatment changes.
option_audit.C: Plausible discipline-silo error; incorrect because self-care and adherence education are multidisciplinary functions and are explicitly compatible with HF nursing care.
option_audit.D: Plausible wait-for-routine-follow-up error; incorrect because new symptom changes require assessment and coordinated response rather than automatic deferral.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable clinical and coordination detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel longitudinal-care actions.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ACC/HFSA and NCSBN source-based reread.
